items.title: Apply fills to a book
items.question: Write `apply_fills(book, fills)`.

widget.how: The first Check downloads the C++ compiler (about 26 MB) and compiles in 10 to 15 s. Later Checks take 1 to 3 s. Check runs 9 hidden tests. Each builds a book, applies some fills, then reads the book's positions.

feedback.correct: Every fill lands on the caller's book.
feedback.generic: Not yet. The results under the editor say which test failed.

byKey.test-1: The quantity did not change. If you loop with `for (Position p : book)`, each `p` is a copy: use `Position& p`.

explain.text: `book` is a plain reference, as the caller's positions change; `fills` is only read, so `const&` also accepts braced lists. The inner loop must use `Position& p`: a copy would absorb the fill and vanish. Buying 200 at 1.85 and selling 50 at 1.90 leaves 150 shares and £275 spent.

items.title: VWAP from a day's fills
items.prose:
A day's executions arrive on `std::cin`: a count `n`, then `n` lines of `qty price`. A quantity of 0 or less is a cancel: skip it. Print the total quantity, then the volume-weighted average price to 4 decimals. That is the total of `qty * price` over total `qty`, or `VWAP n/a` when no shares traded.

```text
QTY 1200
VWAP 101.2375
```
items.question: Complete the program.

widget.prelude: struct Order { long long qty; double px; };
widget.how: The first Check downloads the C++ compiler (about 26 MB) and compiles in 10 to 15 s. Later Checks take 1 to 3 s. Check runs your program 6 times with different orders on std::cin, including cancels, no orders and 2.5 billion shares. A hidden check after your code requires `double vwap(const std::vector<Order>& orders)`.

feedback.correct: Read once, pass by `const&`, print to four decimals.
feedback.generic: Not yet. The results under the editor say which test failed.

byKey.test-4: 2,500,000,000 shares does not fit in an `int`. Keep quantities as `long long`, as `Order` does.

explain.text: The orders are read once into a vector, and every function after that takes `const std::vector<Order>&`, so nothing is copied. The VWAP is total notional over total quantity: 121,485 / 1,200 = 101.2375. With no live orders the quantity is 0, so the program prints n/a instead of dividing by zero.

items.question: Put the stack events of `price_option(100, 95)` in order.

lines.text: Pop `payoff`, returning 0: 90 is below the strike
`main` prints 7.5, then its frame is popped

feedback.correct: At most three frames, pushed and popped in strict order.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. A frame must be popped before the next call from the same caller starts.

explain.text: Each `payoff` call returns before the next starts, so the stack is at most three deep: `main`, `price_option`, `payoff`. Each `payoff` frame, with its `s` and `k`, dies at its return. In one `+` expression the two calls could run in either order; two lines fix it.

items.question: Select all that apply: which `OrderBook` methods should be marked `const`?

options.why: `add` changes the book. The `const` on its parameter protects `o`, not the book.
Cancelling removes an order, so it changes the book.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which methods only read the book?

explain.text: `best_bid` and `depth` only read, so mark them `const`. A pricer holding a `const OrderBook&` can then call them. The compiler checks that they really leave the book alone.

items.prose: A pricer allocates `new double[steps + 1]` per call and forgets the `delete[]`. A calibration calls it 10,000 times a day with `steps = 500`.
items.question: How many MB does a day's calibration leak? Take 1 MB as 1,000,000 bytes.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the doubles per call first: `steps + 1`.

byKey.n: You used 500 doubles per call. The lattice has `steps + 1` = 501.
byKey.one: That is one call. Multiply by 10,000 calls.
byKey.bytes: That is the count in bytes. Divide by 1,000,000.

explain.text: Each call leaks `new double[501]`, 4,008 bytes. 10,000 calls leak 40,080,000 bytes, about 40 MB a day. A `std::vector<double>` member, sized once, would allocate once and never leak.

items.prose: Each snippet ran in this browser build without stopping.
items.question: Select all that apply: which are undefined behaviour?

options.text: `double* r = new double(1.0); delete r; delete r;`

options.why: `at` checks the index and throws `std::out_of_range`. That is a defined, reported error.
A zero-length `new[]` is legal and `delete[]` is its matching free.

feedback.correct: Null read, mismatched delete, double delete.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Separate checked errors from unchecked ones.

explain.text: Here all three undefined lines ran quietly: the null read gave a stray number, and both bad deletes were silent. A desk build with `-fsanitize=address` reports SEGV, alloc-dealloc-mismatch and double-free. `at` and `new double[0]` are defined.

items.question: What does `first` print?

options.text: Anything: `push_back` may move the elements, leaving `first` dangling

options.why: That assumes the elements stay put. A full vector moves them to a bigger buffer, so `first` refers to freed memory.
`first` was bound to the old `px[0]`, not to the last element. And after the move it refers to nothing valid.
It compiles. The compiler cannot know the vector will grow at run time.

feedback.correct: A reference into a vector dies when the vector grows.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Where are the three prices after `push_back` on a full vector?

explain.text: The vector was full, so `push_back` moved its elements to a new buffer and freed the old one. `first` still refers to the old buffer: in this browser it printed 2.93699e-306, and AddressSanitizer reports heap-use-after-free on line 4. Take the reference after the last `push_back`, or store an index.

items.title: Review a colleague's trade utilities

rubric.text: (a) Says the by-value parameter copies the whole blotter on each call and should be `const std::vector<Trade>&`. Finds the `<=` off-by-one read past the end
(a) Says the off-by-one is undefined behaviour: libc++'s check stops it here, while a desk build may silently add garbage
(b) Says `&best` dangles once its local dies at the `}`; proposes returning by value (`std::optional<Trade>` or an index)
(b) Notes the parameter should be `const&`, the loop variable `const Trade&`, and that an empty blotter makes `trades[0]` undefined
(c) Explains that `add_fee` changes a copy and needs `Trade&`
(d) Says the raw `new` makes every caller responsible for exactly one `delete`, and replaces it with `std::unique_ptr<Pricer>` from `std::make_unique`
(e) Gives four corrected functions that compile and match the fixes above
